assertions.text: applying the same documentary requirements to all employees, without regard to national origin or citizenship status, is what the law requires
assertions.note: Same finding as emp_i9: corroborated by Robison Fruit Ranch, Inc. v. United States, 154 F.3d 807 (9th Cir. 1998), but the claim's actual statutory source is 8 U.S.C. section 1324b(a)(6) read with section 1324b(a)(1), not section 1324a, which is the only citation this clause carries.

assertions.text: Form I-9 must be completed within three (3) business days of the employee's first day of work
assertions.note: Same as emp_i9 -- a regulatory deadline (8 C.F.R. section 274a.2(b)(1)(ii)) that CourtListener's case-law index does not carry, and every host that would carry the regulation directly is blocked.

assertions.text: I-9 forms must be retained separately from personnel files

gaps: Same citation gap as emp_i9: the clause's only citation (8 U.S.C. section 1324a) does not name section 1324b, the actual source of the documentary-uniformity claim.

Same unconfirmed premise as emp_i9: Robison's discrimination-requirement holding construed the pre-1996 statute; the current text was not independently fetched to confirm the 1996 amendment reads the way the opinion describes.

sources.title: CourtListener — Robison Fruit Ranch, Inc. v. United States (9th Cir. 1998) 154 F.3d 807

judicialQuotations.case: Robison Fruit Ranch, Inc. v. United States (9th Cir. 1998) 154 F.3d 807
judicialQuotations.quote: We hold that Congress intended a discrimination requirement in the 1990 statute and merely clarified the statute to state that intent in its 1996 amendment. The evidence unquestionably shows that the employment practices in this case did not create additional burdens to any class of applicants or constitute differential treatment of authorized aliens and citizens. There could have been no discrimination, and the petition for review must be granted.
